key_results: WNA1 selectively inhibits complex-bound HDAC1/2 (minimal activity on recombinant enzyme); WNA1 is hydrolyzed by HDAC1–MTA1 complex with product trapped in HDAC1 foot pocket in inositol-hexaphosphate-dependent manner; WNA1 promotes β-catenin stabilization and hair growth in vivo
comments: The foot-pocket-anchored product inhibition mechanism is elegant and provides a template for selective HDAC1/2 targeting; complex-specificity explains why conventional HDAC inhibitors fail to potentiate WNT signaling.

hypotheses.result: Confirmed; HDAC1 mutants with reduced foot pocket ablate WNA1 activity

hypotheses.result: Confirmed; WNA1-induced HDAC1/2 inhibition potentiates WNT/β-catenin pathway
